pairs.difference: B: the console body, which should be painted metal, is one even satin grey like moulded plastic, with soft rounded edges and no scuffs, brushing or panel seams. All ten buttons carry the same lacquered highlight. A: the cart mixes materials. The popcorn is finely lumpy, the glass is thin with a pale streak, the red box is enamel and the awning is matte.
pairs.fix: Make the console read as painted steel: crisper panel edges, faint brushed lines and tiny screws at the corners, and a duller finish on the body so that only the button tops are glossy.

pairs.difference: B: the helmet shell is a seamless pearly satin with almost no fine detail, and the shell, collar and ear disc look like the same plastic. Only the amber visor differs. A: the shoes have a fine dotted mesh on the toe, thin seam lines, a matte rubber sole and slightly shiny laces, so several finishes sit on one object.
pairs.fix: Give the helmet a matte, slightly chalky white shell with fine seam lines, small screws around the collar and ear disc, and a thin soft-rubber gasket around the visor. Keep the gloss to the visor alone.

pairs.difference: B: the UFO hull has mottled, smudgy grey blotches that do not follow the form, like smeared noise rather than brushed metal. The rim edges are soft. A: the player and earbuds are clean, soft-sheen plastic with quiet highlights and crisp small grooves, with no noise on the surfaces.
pairs.fix: Clean the hull into smooth brushed silver with fine, even streaks that follow the curve, one clear soft highlight band and no blotches.

pairs.difference: B: the rocket body is an airbrushed silver gradient and the fins are red satin, with small rivets and one rim line, so the metal is close to a smooth chrome-plastic. A: the submarine is lacquered yellow with copper rings that have warm, varied reflections and small rivets. The two are very close. B is slightly more uniform, but the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Break up the silver body with faint panel seams and slightly duller, brushed areas beside the highlights, and make the fins a matte paint rather than satin.

pairs.difference: A: the white frame, door surround and base all share one smooth satin finish, with almost no seams or wear on the structure and only the soft ground carrying marks. B: the bar has much louder material marking, with speckled concrete, shingles, an embossed pineapple and wet tile. That noise is rougher than the quiet real cards, so the surface evidence is mixed and A is only a slight preference.
pairs.fix: Separate the base materials: matte painted metal panels with thin seams and small bolts on the white frame, slightly rubbery seals around the glass, and a few very fine scuffs near the ground.

pairs.difference: A: the planet and ring are one matte clay with almost no gloss (gloss_share 0.001, below the real range), and the bands are flat colour shapes with no surface change between them. B: the flip-flops mix a matte, finely textured rubber sole with crisp small pimples and a shinier yellow strap, so they have a real gloss range.
pairs.fix: Give the ring a smooth, slightly glossy finish with a thin bright highlight along its edge, and keep the planet matte with fine soft banding, so the two parts read as different materials.

pairs.difference: A: this is the rose arch from the real reference sheet, with crisp petals and leaves, and its high numbers come from the dense foliage. B: the column is believable matte plaster-stone with shallow fluting and a fine crack, against a separate glossy gold plaque. Nothing on the surfaces separates them.

B: the rock has one even, fine sandpaper grain over everything, including the crater walls, so it reads as clay. There is no gloss variation, no chips and no sharper stone edges. A: the scarf is puffy with no weave, but that smooth rubbery cloth matches the real cards, and the badge adds a shinier enamel contrast. Both are weak, so this is a low-confidence call.
pairs.fix: Vary the rock surface: rough pitted patches, smoother worn faces, small sharp chips along the crater rims, and a slight dark shine on the heat-scorched side.

pairs.difference: A: the dish, arms, mount and base are all the same pale matte plastic, so metal does not read as metal. The base plate has only a faint outline and tiny corner dots. B: the sandcastle has sculpted sand edges and grainy dunes beside a shiny plastic bucket, so the gloss contrast is clear.
pairs.fix: Paint the dish as enamel white with a soft sheen, make the arms and base darker bare steel with sharper edges, and add small bolts, thin welds and a little sand dust at the foot.

pairs.difference: A: the fountain has matte sandstone with quiet shading and glassy water, plus fine worn brick around it. B: the bumper car has enamel green paint, a matte rubber bumper and a shiny reflective floor. Both have a clear gloss range and quiet detail at the right scale, so there is no surface reason to choose.

B: the tripod's wood grain is a set of wide, smeary streaks with a glossy varnish that sits on the surface. The cream tube is a blank satin with almost no detail and gloss_share is 0.035, just below the real range. A: the binoculars show fine brushed marks on the metal rim, ribbed grips and a matte green body against a glossy lens.
pairs.fix: Use fine, quiet wood grain running along the legs, a duller oiled finish, a faintly leather-wrapped or matte painted tube, and thin crisp brass bands with a small bright highlight.

pairs.difference: B: the rover body is one soft white satin with blurred, rounded panel lines, and the vents and hatch are moulded-in toy details. Only the tyres change finish. A: the taxi has crisp windscreen wipers, a detailed interior, thin chrome trim and glassy headlamps against enamel paint, so the finishes vary at a fine scale.
pairs.fix: Make the body enamel-painted panels with thin dark seam lines and small screws, add bright bare-metal trim around the lamps and a fine dust film along the lower edges, and keep the tyres matte rubber.

pattern: Generated cards are given away by material sameness more than by any single flaw. Surfaces that should differ (painted metal, bare metal, rubber, seals) collapse into one even satin plastic, as on the console, helmet, dish and rover. Fine detail is moulded in softly instead of drawn crisply: seams and panels are blurred, and small rivets, screws and wear are missing. When texture does appear, it is laid uniformly over the whole object or smeared across the form, as with the UFO's mottled hull, the meteor's even sandpaper grain and the telescope's wide streaky wood. The measured fields rarely separate the pairs, because nearly all values fall inside the real ranges. Caveat: on p04, p05 and p08 the surface evidence alone is thin, and my choice leans on the sci-fi subject matter seen across the test set (one space-themed card per pair, except p07 and p10, which is partly why those two are neither). Those picks are low confidence for that reason.
